transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in today?

Well, I... I came in because I just can't shake this feeling. It's like this heavy, crushing weight that I carry around all the time, from the moment I wake up until I finally manage to fall asleep, if I even do. I just feel like everything that goes wrong, no matter how small or how completely out of my control it might actually be, is entirely my fault. Like, at work—I'm a business operations specialist, and we've had some supply chain hiccups lately. Logically, I know it's a global issue, but I just sit at my desk staring at the spreadsheets, convinced that if I had just been smarter, or worked harder, or anticipated things better, none of it would have happened. I feel like a completely terrible employee, like I'm letting everyone down and they're all just waiting for the right moment to fire me because I'm so incompetent. 

And it's not just work, it's at home too. I bought my house a couple of years ago, which was a huge deal for me, but the other day the water heater broke. Just a normal thing that happens, right? But I just completely fell apart. I sat on the basement floor and cried because I felt like I had ruined the house, like I'm a bad homeowner who doesn't deserve to have nice things. I just keep thinking that I deserve to lose everything I've worked so hard for, my job, my house, everything, because I'm just fundamentally flawed and everything I touch gets ruined. It's just exhausting, feeling this guilty and worthless all the time, over every little thing.
How long have you been feeling this way?

Well, it's... it's been a really long time. I've actually been trying to pinpoint exactly when it started, because you know, you always want to find a reason or a starting point, right? Like some big event that triggered it all. But looking back at my calendar and just thinking about when I really stopped caring about things... it's been right about two years and one month. 

I remember because it was shortly after I finally got all my boxes unpacked at the new house. You would think I would have been so excited, right? Decorating, having friends over for a housewarming, all that normal stuff. But instead, that was when this huge, heavy cloud just kind of rolled in and never left. The depression, and just... this complete loss of interest in absolutely everything I used to enjoy. Like, I used to love going to farmers' markets on weekends, or even just reading a book on the porch, but for the last two years and a month, I just haven't cared. I haven't wanted to do any of it. 

It's just been this endless, exhausting stretch of waking up and feeling nothing but that heavy sadness and guilt. It's like the color just completely drained out of my life twenty-five months ago, and I keep waiting for it to come back, but it just doesn't. I keep thinking maybe if I just push through it'll lift, but two years is a really, really long time to just feel this empty and uninterested in your own life, you know? I just don't know how much longer I can keep pretending I'm fine at work and everywhere else when this feeling has been sitting on my chest for over two years.
Have you had thoughts of ending your life or killing yourself?

No, I... I haven't. I mean, I know that's a common thing when people are this depressed, and I completely understand why you have to ask. It makes sense. But for me, it's not really about wanting to die, it's just... it's more about not wanting to feel this way anymore. I don't sit around making plans or thinking about how I would do it, or anything like that. It's not that I want to end my life, it's just that the life I'm living right now feels so incredibly heavy and impossible to manage. 

Like, sometimes I just wish I could go to sleep and not wake up for a week, just to get a break from the constant guilt and the feeling that I'm ruining everything I touch. But that's not the same as wanting to kill myself, right? I still have this tiny, rational part of my brain that knows I have a house to pay for, and my job, even if I feel like I'm terrible at it, it's still my responsibility. I just... I don't want to die. I just really, really want the color to come back. I want to wake up and not feel like a burden to the entire world. But no, I haven't had any actual thoughts of ending my life. I just want the life I have to stop hurting so much, if that makes any sense at all.
During these past two years, have you had any period lasting two months or more when you felt mostly like yourself and the depression was largely gone?

Well, um... no. Not really. I mean, I've thought about that too, trying to find some stretch of time where things felt normal again, where I felt like the old me, but... looking back over the whole two years and a month, it's just been this constant, heavy blanket over everything. The low mood, the completely losing interest in my garden, my friends, my house... it's just been there for almost the entire time since this whole thing started. 

There have been a few days here and there, maybe a week at the absolute most, where I felt like I could function a little better. Like, maybe I managed to get through a whole workday without feeling like I was going to burst into tears at my desk, or I actually managed to unload the dishwasher instead of just staring at it. But those are just tiny little blips, you know? They never last. It's never been two whole months. Not even close. It's more like... I get a tiny gasp of air, just enough to think, 'Oh, maybe it's finally lifting,' and then, bam, the weight is right back on my chest and I'm right back to feeling completely empty and worthless. So, no, there hasn't been any real break from it. It's just been this one long, exhausting stretch with barely any relief at all.
How much has your depression interfered with your ability to work and manage your usual daily responsibilities?

Well, it's... it's definitely taken a toll. I mean, I try really hard to keep it together, especially at work, because I'm a business operations specialist and my job is literally about keeping things running smoothly, you know? But lately, it's just been so incredibly difficult to focus. I'll be staring at a spreadsheet, and it's like my brain just refuses to process the numbers. I've made enough little mistakes—missing a deadline here, messing up a report there—that my supervisor actually pulled me aside last week to check in on my performance. She was nice about it, asking if everything was okay, but it was just so humiliating because I know I'm not doing my best work. I'm still showing up every day, still trying to push through, but it takes every ounce of energy I have just to do the bare minimum.

And then I get home, and I'm just completely drained. I have this townhouse that I bought a couple of years ago, and I used to take so much pride in it. I'd keep everything spotless, but now... I mean, I let it get so much messier than I can stand. There are dishes piled up in the sink, laundry sitting in baskets for weeks, and I just look at it and feel this overwhelming sense of failure, but I can't bring myself to actually clean it. 

And my social life is basically nonexistent at this point. My friends will text me to go out for dinner or grab a coffee, and I just... I make up excuses. I'll tell them I'm too tired from work, or I have a headache, but the truth is I just don't have the energy to sit there and pretend to be happy and engaged. I've missed so many social plans over the last year that some of them have even stopped asking. So, yeah, I'm still functioning on some level—I'm still working and paying my bills—but it just feels like I'm wading through molasses every single day, and keeping up with even the most basic responsibilities takes so much more effort than it ever used to.
How has your sleep been during this period?

Sleep... oh, sleep is just a mess. It really is. I mean, I am so incredibly exhausted all day long, like I was saying about work and the house, so you'd think the second my head hits the pillow, I'd just be out cold, right? But that's not what happens at all. I try to be disciplined about it, I really do. I get into bed, I turn off my phone, I make the room dark, but then I just... I just lie there. For hours and hours. 

Most nights I'm just lying awake in the dark, and it's so quiet that every little sound is magnified. I just listen to the house settle. You know how those newer townhouses are, they make those little popping and creaking noises in the walls as the temperature drops? I just lie there listening to the floors creak, watching the clock tick closer to midnight, then one in the morning, just begging my brain to shut off so I can get some relief. 

And then, when I finally do manage to drift off, which takes forever, it's like my body just refuses to actually stay asleep. I almost always wake up around three or four in the morning. My eyes just pop open, and I know instantly that it's over. I try to roll over, I try adjusting the blankets, I try all those deep breathing things to just get a little more rest, but I just can't get back to sleep before I have to actually get up for work. So I just end up lying there for another two or three hours, dreading the alarm, knowing I have to go into the office and try to function on practically zero rest. It's just this agonizing cycle every single night, and it makes everything the next day feel ten times heavier than it already is.
During this period, have you noticed any significant change in your appetite or weight?

Well, my appetite... it's just been all over the place, really. It's like my stomach and my brain aren't even communicating anymore. Most days, especially when I'm at the office and trying so hard just to focus on my spreadsheets and not make any more mistakes, I just completely forget to eat. Or maybe not forget, but the thought of actually preparing a meal, or even just going down to the cafeteria to buy something, feels like climbing a mountain. So I just skip real meals during the day. I'll sit there at my desk and drink coffee after coffee, just trying to stay awake because of how terrible my sleep is, like I was telling you. 

And then I'll get home to my messy house, and I'm so drained that I can't even fathom turning on the stove or chopping a vegetable. So I just end up grabbing whatever requires zero effort. I've basically been living on toast. Just plain toast, or maybe I'll find a granola bar in the pantry. It's whatever is easiest and fastest so I can just go lie down. 

And because of all this, I've definitely noticed a change in my weight. I haven't actually stepped on a scale—I don't think I even own one, to be honest—but I can feel it in my clothes. My work trousers, the ones I wear all the time, they're definitely looser around the waist. I have to pull my belt a notch tighter than I used to, and my blouses just sort of hang off me now. It's not like I'm trying to lose weight or anything, it's just a byproduct of having zero energy or desire to actually feed myself properly. It just feels like another thing I'm failing at, you know? Like, I can't even manage to eat a normal dinner like a normal person. It's just coffee and toast, day in and day out.
During these two years, have there been at least two weeks when your depressed mood or loss of interest was present nearly every day along with several of the other symptoms you described?

Well, yeah, definitely. I mean, it's not just two weeks here or there, it's... it's been pretty constant. I actually remember exactly when it started getting really bad, because it was right around the time I was finalizing the paperwork for my townhouse. So that was, what, just over two years ago now? Maybe two years and one month? I remember I was supposed to be so excited, you know? Buying your first place at twenty-five, that's a huge milestone, and my parents were so proud, and my friends wanted to throw a housewarming party. But I just... I couldn't feel it. I remember sitting on the floor of the empty living room surrounded by boxes, and I just felt this crushing weight, this absolute emptiness, and I just cried. 

And honestly, since that day, it really hasn't lifted. So yes, definitely more than two weeks. It's been practically every single day for those two years and a month. I mean, sure, there are days where maybe I can fake a smile a little better at the office, or days where I manage to actually put a dish in the dishwasher instead of just leaving it on the counter, but that underlying feeling? That complete lack of joy or interest in anything, combined with the exhaustion and the not sleeping and the eating nothing but toast? That's just been my reality, day in and day out. It's like a heavy wet blanket that I've been dragging around with me for over two years, and it just never dries out. So, yeah, finding a two-week period where all of this was happening together is... well, it's basically just picking any random two weeks out of the last twenty-five months.
Over the past two years, has your depressed mood been present for most of the day on most days?

Yeah, exactly. Like I was just saying, if I really sit down and look back at the whole timeline... that low mood and the total loss of interest in everything, it's just been there for almost the entire time since this whole thing started. It's really most of the day, every day. It's not like I have these long stretches where I feel like my old self again. 

I mean, there have been these very, very brief periods where maybe I could function just a little bit better. Like, maybe for a day or two, I'll actually be able to answer my emails at work without staring at the screen for twenty minutes first, or I'll manage to fold a basket of laundry that's been sitting in the corner of my bedroom for three weeks. I'll think, oh, maybe I'm finally snapping out of it, maybe this is the turning point. But it never is. It's just a tiny blip, a drop in the bucket, really, and then I'm right back down into that same heavy, miserable feeling where I just don't care about anything at all. 

So when you ask if it's most of the day on most days, absolutely. It's just been this endless stretch of feeling completely empty. I mean, when you really think about how many days are in two years, to feel like that for almost all of them, from the minute I wake up at four in the morning until I finally manage to fall asleep... it's just exhausting to even talk about, honestly. It's just always there.
Before this current two-year period began, had you ever experienced a distinct period of depression like this before?

No, I don't think so... I mean, looking back, before I bought the townhouse and all this started, I was actually doing really well. I was just a normal person, you know? I was twenty-five, I had my degree, I was working my way up at the company, doing all the things you're supposed to do. I mean, sure, I'd get stressed out sometimes. Like, during end-of-quarter reporting, I'd feel overwhelmed, or if I had a fight with a friend, I'd be sad for a day or two. But it was never anything like this. It was just normal life stuff. 

I never had this... this feeling of just being completely drained and hollowed out. I used to actually enjoy things. I used to go to brunch with my friends on Sundays, and I used to go to spin class, and I actually cared about how my apartment looked. I would never have let laundry sit for three weeks back then. I was organized, I was on top of things. So, no, before two years ago, I never had a period where I felt like this. This whole dark cloud, this heavy blanket thing... it's all new since I moved into the townhouse. Before that, I was just... me. And I really miss being me, honestly. I don't even recognize the person I've been for the last two years.

I've basically been living on toast. Just plain toast, or maybe I'll find a granola bar in the pantry. It's whatever is easiest and fastest so I can just go lie down. 

And because of all this, I've definitely noticed a change in my weight. I haven't actually stepped on a scale—I don't think I even own one, to be honest—but I can feel it in my clothes. My work trousers, the ones I wear all the time, they're definitely looser around the waist. I have to pull my belt a notch tighter than I used to, and my blouses just sort of hang off me now. It's not like I'm trying to lose weight or anything, it's just a byproduct of having zero energy or desire to actually feed myself properly. It just feels like another thing I'm failing at, you know? Like, I can't even manage to eat a normal dinner like a normal person. It's just coffee and toast, day in and day out.

inference.note: This turn confirms additional major depressive symptoms (insomnia, decreased appetite/weight, fatigue, concentration impairment) and significant occupational and social impairment, supporting both persistent depressive disorder and a concurrent moderate major depressive episode.

doctor.intent: Clarify whether the chronic depressive symptoms have met full major depressive episode criteria continuously, distinguishing persistent depressive disorder from a single moderate major depressive episode.
doctor.question: During these two years, have there been at least two weeks when your depressed mood or loss of interest was present nearly every day along with several of the other symptoms you described?

target_item.name: Depressive Episode Duration
target_item.manifestation: The depression and loss of interest have been with me for about two years and one month.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if the depressive symptoms have been present concurrently for at least two weeks, which is inquiring about the duration and presence of the depressive episode.

patient.answer:
Well, yeah, definitely. I mean, it's not just two weeks here or there, it's... it's been pretty constant. I actually remember exactly when it started getting really bad, because it was right around the time I was finalizing the paperwork for my townhouse. So that was, what, just over two years ago now? Maybe two years and one month? I remember I was supposed to be so excited, you know? Buying your first place at twenty-five, that's a huge milestone, and my parents were so proud, and my friends wanted to throw a housewarming party. But I just... I couldn't feel it. I remember sitting on the floor of the empty living room surrounded by boxes, and I just felt this crushing weight, this absolute emptiness, and I just cried. 

And honestly, since that day, it really hasn't lifted. So yes, definitely more than two weeks. It's been practically every single day for those two years and a month. I mean, sure, there are days where maybe I can fake a smile a little better at the office, or days where I manage to actually put a dish in the dishwasher instead of just leaving it on the counter, but that underlying feeling? That complete lack of joy or interest in anything, combined with the exhaustion and the not sleeping and the eating nothing but toast? That's just been my reality, day in and day out. It's like a heavy wet blanket that I've been dragging around with me for over two years, and it just never dries out. So, yeah, finding a two-week period where all of this was happening together is... well, it's basically just picking any random two weeks out of the last twenty-five months.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the depression has been persistently present most of the day on most days for the full two-year period, supporting persistent depressive disorder over a single major depressive episode.
doctor.question: Over the past two years, has your depressed mood been present for most of the day on most days?

target_item.name: Additional Requirement 2
target_item.manifestation: Looking back, the low mood and loss of interest have been there for almost the whole time since this started, with only brief periods where I could function a little better.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether the depressed mood has been present for the majority of the illness duration (over the past two years), which corresponds to the requirement that the depressive episode is present for the majority of the total duration of the illness.

patient.answer:
Yeah, exactly. Like I was just saying, if I really sit down and look back at the whole timeline... that low mood and the total loss of interest in everything, it's just been there for almost the entire time since this whole thing started. It's really most of the day, every day. It's not like I have these long stretches where I feel like my old self again. 

I mean, there have been these very, very brief periods where maybe I could function just a little bit better. Like, maybe for a day or two, I'll actually be able to answer my emails at work without staring at the screen for twenty minutes first, or I'll manage to fold a basket of laundry that's been sitting in the corner of my bedroom for three weeks. I'll think, oh, maybe I'm finally snapping out of it, maybe this is the turning point. But it never is. It's just a tiny blip, a drop in the bucket, really, and then I'm right back down into that same heavy, miserable feeling where I just don't care about anything at all. 

So when you ask if it's most of the day on most days, absolutely. It's just been this endless stretch of feeling completely empty. I mean, when you really think about how many days are in two years, to feel like that for almost all of them, from the minute I wake up at four in the morning until I finally manage to fall asleep... it's just exhausting to even talk about, honestly. It's just always there.

doctor.intent: Determine whether this is a first depressive episode or whether there were prior distinct depressive episodes, which helps distinguish persistent depressive disorder from a single major depressive episode.
doctor.question: Before this current two-year period began, had you ever experienced a distinct period of depression like this before?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about my psychiatric history prior to the current episode, which is not covered by my symptom profile.

patient.answer:
No, I don't think so... I mean, looking back, before I bought the townhouse and all this started, I was actually doing really well. I was just a normal person, you know? I was twenty-five, I had my degree, I was working my way up at the company, doing all the things you're supposed to do. I mean, sure, I'd get stressed out sometimes. Like, during end-of-quarter reporting, I'd feel overwhelmed, or if I had a fight with a friend, I'd be sad for a day or two. But it was never anything like this. It was just normal life stuff. 

I never had this... this feeling of just being completely drained and hollowed out. I used to actually enjoy things. I used to go to brunch with my friends on Sundays, and I used to go to spin class, and I actually cared about how my apartment looked. I would never have let laundry sit for three weeks back then. I was organized, I was on top of things. So, no, before two years ago, I never had a period where I felt like this. This whole dark cloud, this heavy blanket thing... it's all new since I moved into the townhouse. Before that, I was just... me. And I really miss being me, honestly. I don't even recognize the person I've been for the last two years.
